ai.description: *Hemidactylus malcolmsmithi* reaches 50 mm SVL. It is pale grey-brown with dark dorsal crossbars and possesses strongly keeled, trihedral tubercles. Its subdigital lamellae are divided.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus malcolmsmithi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, flattened tubercles forming a lateral fold along its flanks.
ai.habitat: Malcolm Smith's Gecko inhabits rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn areas within dry deciduous forests, typically found at elevations between 300 and 900 meters.
ai.behavior: Malcolm Smith's gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its rocky habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus malcolmsmithi* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: Malcolm Smith's Gecko is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at high elevations.
